summary: Columns designed as short braced C25/30 members (fixed base, 3.0 m clear height, slenderness < limits per BS 8110 cl 3.8.1.3) using the simplified axial capacity expression N = 0.4 fcu Ac + 0.75 fy Asc (cl 3.8.4.3). All factored axial loads (124–339 kN) are well below the capacity of a 230×230 mm section with minimum longitudinal steel (~0.8% Ac, 4T16), so this minimum practical section governs for C1–C4 and C6–C9; C5 (highest load, 338.9 kN) is upsized to 250×250 mm with 4T20 for robustness and cover requirements (40 mm main cover, 50 mm assumed at base construction joint). Beams are 250×450 mm C25/30 sections designed for the stated ULS moments and shears (loads per BS 6399-1 UDL 11.98 kN/m² factored 1.4Gk+1.6Qk). Flexural design used the BS 8110 singly-reinforced rectangular stress-block method (K = M/bd²fcu, z = d[0.5+√(0.25−K/0.9)] ≤0.95d) with d ≈ 410 mm (25 mm cover, 12 mm link, 20 mm bar assumed): M = 83.7 kNm beams (B1,B2,B5,B6 and mirrored B7,B8,B11,B12) require As≈635 mm² → 3T20 (942 mm²); M = 78.8 kNm beams (B3,B4,B9,B10) require As≈593 mm² → 3T16 (603 mm²). Shear design (cl 3.4.5) gave v ≈ 0.83–0.86 N/mm² against vc ≈ 0.55–0.60 N/mm² for the provided steel ratio; since v−vc <0.4 N/mm², nominal/minimum shear links govern: 8 mm mild/high-yield 2-leg links at 300 mm c/c (≤0.75d) throughout. All beams and columns detailed with high-yield T-bars (fy = 410 N/mm², BS 4449) and covers of 25 mm (beams) / 40 mm (columns, 50 mm at base) per BS 8110-1:1997.
